rubrics.justification: Generally cautious and mostly consistent with the image as a blastocyst with limited clarity, but it overinterprets some features (organized TE, zona thinning assessment) and questions the reported 3AA/expanded status without strong visual certainty from this single frame.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, endometrium, male factor, BMI, lifestyle, and first-cycle status with embryo quality and prognosis.

Reasoning is structured and mostly logical, with conclusions tied to age, lining, and embryo quality; minor tension exists between calling the case good prognosis while also suggesting the grade may be optimistic.

Recommendations are largely evidence-based and aligned with standard IVF practice, including SET in a young good-prognosis patient and avoiding overreaction after one failed transfer; minor grading terminology discussion is somewhat imprecise.
Provides practical next steps for transfer management, follow-up, and contingency planning, though some suggestions remain broad rather than highly case-specific.
